'''''Sporobolus virginicus''''', known by numerous common names including '''seashore dropseed''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=SPVI3|taxon=Sporobolus virginicus|accessdate=27 November 2015}}</ref> '''marine couch''', '''sand couch''', '''salt couch grass''', '''saltwater couch''', '''coastal rat-tail grass''', and '''nioaka''', is a species of [[Poaceae|grass]] with a wide distribution.

==Description==
It is a [[Rhizome|spreading]] perennial [[Tussock (grass)|tussock grass]] from {{cvt|10|to|50|cm|abbr=on}} in height. Its flowers are green or purple. It reproduces asexually by use of both [[stolon]]s and [[rhizome]]s.<ref name="FloraBase 635">{{FloraBase | name = ''Sporobolus virginicus'' (L.) Kunth | id = 635}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
It was originally published by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in 1753, under the name ''Agrostis virginicus''. It was transferred into ''[[Sporobolus]]'' by [[Karl Sigismund Kunth]] in 1829. It has a great many synonyms.<ref name="APNI 42563"/><ref name=gbif/>

At least in Australia, the species can grade between narrow and broad leaf forms.<ref name="PlantNET"/>

==Distribution and habitat==
It grows in [[Australia]], [[New Zealand]], many [[Pacific Islands]], the [[Caribbean]], [[Africa]], [[India]], [[China]] and [[Indonesia]]. It is widespread in Australia,<ref>p24 ''It is the most wildly distributed saltmarsh plant in Australia'' {{Citation | author1=Saintilan, Neil | author2=CSIRO | title=Australian saltmarsh ecology | date=2009 | publisher=CSIRO Publishing | isbn=978-0-643-09684-4 }}</ref> occurring in every state.<ref name="PlantNET">{{NSW Flora Online | genus = Sporobolus | species = virginicus | author = S. W. L. Jacobs & K. L. McClay}}</ref>
